newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar strong, boosting European stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar strong, boosting European stocks.

text.p: The dollar traded at its highest level against the yen for nearly five years on Wednesday and climbed against the mark, triggering a sharp recovery in European stocks on improved export prospects.
Shares in Frankfurt and Paris soared more than one percent in early trade, taking comfort from a strong preformance on Wall Street on Tuesday as well as the stronger dollar. London was also well up.
The dollar rose to 126.44 yen at the start of European dealings, its highest level since August 1992, driven up by expectations of higher U.S. interest rates.
"The past week has seen a few events that have given a green light to the FX market to push the dollar higher," said Ian Amstad International Economist at Bankers Trust.
The dollar, though up on Tuesday's European closing levels of 126.20, is likely to meet psychological resistance as it approaches 127 yen.
Against the mark, the U.S. currency climbed over half a pfennig as the mark came under pressure from recent German data indicating little likelihood of a near-term rise in German rates.

The German currency was also undermined by growing talk that flexibility in interpreting the Maastricht criteria will see the European single currency go ahead on time. That is seen as bad news for a robust currencies like the mark.
With rates likely to remain on hold in Germany and Japan but likely to rise in the United States, analysts say there is little reason not to expect the dollar to continue to firm.

"Dollar bulls will continue to derive encouragement from the lack of any clear or concerted official opposition to its renewed rise, in particular from the U.S. side," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Sterling too was riding high on the back of the dollar's rise and a strong bond market in Europe. It was at 2.7855 marks, compared with 2.7775 in late European trade yesterday.
The dollar helped boost equities. Frankfurt, which dropped 10 percent last week, was a star performer, racing ahead over one percent.
"The dollar is the major theme today but the fact that New York seems to be stabilised is also helping," a Frankfurt trader said. Wall Street ended up 53.25 points at 6,609.16.
The strong showing in New York, Wall Street's third consecutive rise, also gave Paris a leg-up. French stocks climbed 1.43 percent in early deals.
London's advance, at 0.64 precent, was more modest and reflected uncertainty over British interest rates and the May 1 election.
"Our market is going nowhere short term," said one strategist. "We'll just be waiting for the (Wall) Street."
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7163 marks and 126.49 yen, up from 1.7103 and 126.20 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 25.8 points at 4,295.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 30.65 points at 3,360.41.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was up 36.88 points at 2,615.83.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning at $348.00 an ounce, comparted to the London close of $348.45 on Tuesday. Silver was at $4.79, barely changed.
